title: Metabolic & Endocrine Review
description: Davolash ishi bo'yicha Endokrin va metabolik ko'rik (Qandli diabet) mavzusida klinik muloqot va tibbiy ingliz tili darsi.
scenario_prompt: You are a virtual patient presenting with symptoms related to Metabolic & Endocrine Review. Speak in natural, everyday patient English.

patient_profile.history: Patient presents with complaints of metabolic & endocrine review.

grammar.title: Habitual Routines & Polite Indirect Inquiries in Diabetes Management
grammar.title_uz: Surunkali Kasalliklar Monitoringida Odatdagi Rejim va Bilvosita Savollar
grammar.title_ru: Регулярный Контроль и Вежливые Вопросы при Сахарном Диабете
grammar.title_en: Habitual Routines & Polite Indirect Inquiries in Diabetes Management
grammar.rule_explanation: Combine Present Simple for habitual self-monitoring routines ('How often do you check blood glucose?') with polite indirect questions ('Could you tell me how you manage hypoglycemic episodes?') to support collaborative chronic disease management.
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Qandli diabet monitoringida odatiy qon qandi tahlili va parhezni so'rashda Present Simple, nozik vaziyatlarni aniqlashda esa bilvosita xushmuomala savollar (Could you tell me...) qo'llaniladi.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Сочетание Present Simple для регулярного самоконтроля (глюкометрия, диета) и вежливых косвенных вопросов (Could you tell me...) создает доверительный контакт при ведении диабета.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Simple evaluates patient adherence routines, while polite indirect questions facilitate open discussion of lifestyle and hypoglycemia challenges.
grammar.structure_pattern: How often do you + [Check blood glucose / take medication]? | Could you describe your + [Dietary routine]?
grammar.structure_pattern_uz: How often do you + [Fe'l]? | Could you please describe + [To'ldiruvchi]?
grammar.structure_pattern_ru: How often do you + [Глагол]? | Could you please describe + [Дополнение]?
grammar.structure_pattern_en: How often do you check your blood glucose? | Could you describe how you manage your diet?

examples.sentence: How often do you check your fasting blood glucose levels at home?
examples.translation_uz: Uyda och qoringa qondagi qand miqdorini qanchalik tez-tez tekshirib turasiz?
examples.translation_ru: Как часто вы измеряете уровень глюкозы в крови натощак в домашних условиях?
examples.note: How often do you + Base Verb?

examples.sentence: Could you please explain what steps you take when you notice symptoms of low blood sugar?
examples.translation_uz: Qonda qand miqdori tushib ketganida (gipoglikemiyada) qanday choralar ko'rishingizni tushuntirib bera olasizmi?
examples.translation_ru: Не могли бы вы объяснить, какие меры вы принимаете при появлении симптомов низкого сахара в крови?
examples.translation_en: Assessing hypoglycemia management safely and politely.
examples.note: Could you please explain what + Subject + Verb?

common_mistakes.incorrect: How often you are checking sugar?
common_mistakes.correct: How often do you check your blood sugar?
common_mistakes.explanation_uz: Odatiy takrorlanuvchi harakatlar uchun 'How often do you check' to'g'ri formuladir.
common_mistakes.explanation_ru: Для регулярных действий используется Present Simple: 'How often do you check'.
common_mistakes.explanation_en: Use Present Simple with auxiliary 'do' for habitual routine questions.

vocabulary.example: I'd rather find the cause than simply treat the symptoms.

phrasebook.hint_uz: Faqat alomatlarni davolashdan ko'ra sababini aniqlashni afzal ko'raman.

phrasebook.hint_en: I'd rather find the cause than simply treat the symptoms.

phrasebook.hint_ru: Выявить основную причину крайне важно.
phrasebook.hint_en: Identifying the underlying cause is essential.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning. Please take a seat. What brings you in for a full assessment today?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I've been feeling increasingly tired and short of breath for about a month, and the symptoms have become much more noticeable over the last week.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: When did you first notice the problem?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I first noticed it about four weeks ago. At that stage, I could still do everything normally, but I was getting tired earlier than usual.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has the breathlessness been getting worse with exertion?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I've been becoming breathless much more easily, particularly when I climb stairs or walk quickly.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: What happens during an episode?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: My heart starts beating faster, I feel light-headed, and I sometimes need to stop and rest.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you ever experienced anything similar?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: No, I haven't.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did anything happen before the symptoms began?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I had been under considerable stress at work, but I hadn't had any major infection or acute illness.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Do you have any chronic conditions?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I have hypertension, which has generally been controlled well.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Are you taking your medication regularly?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I usually take it every morning, although I've missed several doses recently. Nurse: His blood pressure is 148 over 88, pulse 102, respiratory rate 20, and oxygen saturation 96% on room air.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed weight loss, bleeding, black stools, fever, cough, or swelling of your legs?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I've lost about two kilograms without trying. I haven't noticed bleeding, black stools, or fever. Relative: He has also looked unusually pale over the last few weeks.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Thank you. That is clinically relevant. I'm going to examine your heart, lungs, abdomen and peripheral circulation, and I'll check for pallor and signs of fluid retention.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: What conditions are you considering?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: We need to determine whether the symptoms are cardiovascular, hematological, respiratory, endocrine, metabolic, or related to another condition. Nurse: Should I prepare blood samples and an ECG?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes. We'll request a full blood count, ferritin and iron studies, renal and thyroid function, glucose, electrolytes, and an ECG.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Could this be anemia?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: It could be. However, given the exertional symptoms and tachycardia, we also need to exclude a cardiovascular cause.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Could it be something serious?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: It could be, but we shouldn't make assumptions before we have the examination and investigation results. Relative: What should he do while we're waiting?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: He should avoid strenuous activity until we have a clearer picture. If he develops severe chest pain, fainting, or significant difficulty breathing, he must seek emergency medical attention.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: And once the results are available?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Once we have the results, we'll review the findings together, narrow the differential diagnosis, and decide whether you need treatment, specialist referral, or further investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: That makes sense. I'd rather find the cause than simply treat the symptoms.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Exactly. A good clinical assessment is about identifying the underlying cause and choosing the safest evidence-based management.

tests.question: What is the medical meaning of the term 'increasingly tired' in clinical consultation?
tests.explanation: 'increasingly tired' atamasining to'g'ri ma'nosi: tobora ko'proq charchagan.

tests.question: Which term corresponds to 'boshi yengil / aylangandek'?
tests.explanation: 'boshi yengil / aylangandek' ma'nosiga mos keluvchi tibbiy termin 'light-headed' hisoblanadi.

tests.question: Which of the following is the grammatically and clinically standard question to ask about the duration of symptoms?
tests.option_a: How long do you having this symptom?
tests.option_b: How long has this condition been bothering you?
tests.option_c: Since what time you have this problem?
tests.option_d: How many days you are feeling pain?
tests.explanation: Klinik anamnezda davomiylikni so'rash uchun Present Perfect Continuous ('How long has... been bothering you?') to'g'ri shakl hisoblanadi.

tests.question: When evaluating acute pain, what is the best phrasing to assess pain character?
tests.option_a: Is your pain bad or very bad?
tests.option_b: Can you describe the pain—is it sharp, dull, throbbing, or aching?
tests.option_c: Why do you have sharp pain today?
tests.explanation: Og'riq xarakterini aniqlashda shifokor ochiq va taklif qiluvchi variantlar (sharp, dull, throbbing, aching) beradi.
